response: Yes, radiotherapy of the primary rectal cancer can affect prognosis after pelvic exenteration for recurrent rectal cancer. Studies have shown that patients who received radiotherapy for their primary rectal cancer tend to have a poorer prognosis and lower survival rates after pelvic exenteration for recurrent disease, compared to those who did not receive radiotherapy. This is likely due to the increased risk of complications and reduced effectiveness of salvage surgery in irradiated tissues.
